{{short description|Statement about the representability of zero by odd degree forms}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Birch's theorem''',<ref>{{cite journal
| first=B. J. | last=Birch | authorlink=Bryan John Birch
| title=Homogeneous forms of odd degree in a large number of variables
| journal=[[Mathematika]]
| volume=4
| pages=102–105
| date=1957
| issue=2 | doi=10.1112/S0025579300001145}}</ref> named for [[Bryan John Birch]], is a statement about the representability of zero by odd degree forms.

==Statement of Birch's theorem==
Let ''K'' be an [[algebraic number field]], ''k'', ''l'' and ''n'' be [[natural number]]s, ''r''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''r''<sub>''k''</sub> be odd natural numbers, and ''f''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''f''<sub>''k''</sub> be [[homogeneous polynomial]]s with [[coefficient]]s in ''K'' of [[degree of a polynomial|degrees]] ''r''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''r''<sub>''k''</sub> respectively in ''n'' variables. Then there exists a number ''ψ''(''r''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''r''<sub>''k''</sub>,&nbsp;''l'',&nbsp;''K'') such that if
:<math>n \ge \psi(r_1,\ldots,r_k,l,K)</math>
then there exists an ''l''-[[dimension (vector space)|dimensional]] [[vector subspace]] ''V'' of ''K''<sup>''n''</sup> such that
:<math>f_1(x) = \cdots = f_k(x) = 0 \text{ for all } x \in V.</math>

==Remarks==
The [[mathematical proof|proof]] of the theorem is by [[mathematical induction|induction]] over the maximal degree of the forms ''f''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''f''<sub>''k''</sub>. Essential to the proof is a special case, which can be proved by an application of the [[Hardy–Littlewood circle method]], of the theorem which states that if ''n'' is sufficiently large and ''r'' is odd, then the equation

:<math>c_1x_1^r+\cdots+c_nx_n^r=0,\quad c_i \in \mathbb{Z},\ i=1,\ldots,n</math>

has a solution in [[integer]]s ''x''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''x''<sub>''n''</sub>, not all of which are&nbsp;0.

The restriction to odd ''r'' is necessary, since even degree forms, such as [[Quadratic_form#Definiteness_of_a_quadratic_form|positive definite quadratic form]]s, may take the value 0 only at the origin.
